Subject: Request: VAT proration and reverse-charge split for Q3 invoices

Hi Jordan,

Hope you’re well — quick billing ask from our side as we close Q3. We recently moved a portion of our EU usage to our Irish entity (ClearSky Ireland Ltd., EORI IE12345678) effective 2026-09-15. Our accounting team sees the Q3 invoice (INV-202609) issued to ClearSky Ltd. and would like the VAT handling adjusted:

- Reverse-charge should apply for the Ireland usage portion (service supplied to an EU business) and reflected as a separate line so our tax engine can reconcile correctly.
- The remainder (UK/other EU) should keep the original VAT treatment.

Can Redwood produce prorated invoice lines for the September billing period and a short ledger mapping (GL codes) so our AP can match proof of reverse-charge? We require the VAT ID validation result for ClearSky Ireland (we’ve attached the ID in the drive link below).

Attachments: invoice-INV-202609.pdf (pdf)
Related link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cRC-matrix

We’re on a tight close — would appreciate an ETA by tomorrow EOD EU time.

Thanks,
Asha Kapoor

Subject: Re: Request: VAT proration and reverse-charge split for Q3 invoices

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear summary and the drive link. We can do the prorated split and provide the ledger mapping. Quick clarifying points so we scope correctly:

1) Confirmed dates: we’ll prorate based on usage dates you provided (Irish entity effective 2026-09-15).
2) VAT ID validation: we will run a VIES check and include the validation string/result on the invoice line item. If VIES returns valid, reverse-charge will be shown with a zero VAT amount and a note \"reverse-charge - art. 194\". If invalid, we’ll show VAT charged and flag for manual follow-up.
3) Invoice format: propose we issue a corrected invoice set with three lines: (a) pre-09-15 usage (original VAT treatment), (b) 09-15 -> 09-30 Ireland usage (reverse-charge line with VAT ID validation), (c) any adjustments/rounding.

Vanessa — can your team confirm the GL/ledger codes and whether we should use a single credit note + reissue, or create a new split invoice (preferred for ClearSky AP clarity)? Ben, please prepare the accounting artifact if we go with a split invoice.

Asha — ETA target: internal confirmation today, updated invoice PDFs by 2026-10-08 18:00 CET.

Jordan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

On Thu, 7 Oct 2026 at 15:05, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Vanessa — can your team confirm the GL/ledger codes and whether we should use a single credit note + reissue, or create a new split invoice (preferred for ClearSky AP clarity)?

Jordan — follow-up with proposed ledger mapping and preferred flow below. CCing Asha for visibility.

Proposed flow (preferred):
- Create a corrected invoice set: issue a credit note equal to the original full invoice amount and issue two invoices: 
  1) INV-202610-1 (pre-2026-09-15 usage) — original VAT treatment applied where required.
  2) INV-202610-2 (2026-09-15 -> 2026-09-30 Ireland portion) — reverse-charge line, VAT 0.00, include VIES validation token and \"Reverse-charge - customer liable\" notation.
- Ledger/GL mapping (example):
  - Sales Revenue: 4000-RD (original income)
  - Reverse-Charge (IRL): 4720-RC (zero-rated VAT lines, reverse-charge memo)
  - VAT Liability: 2100-VAT (only populated on lines where VAT charged)
  - Credit Note: CN-202610-RD (applies to 4000-RD)

Attachments: rc-decision-matrix.xlsx (xls) — contains the VIES check steps and example invoice line wording.

Notes:
- If VIES returns \"valid\" for ClearSky Ireland, we will mark INV-202610-2 appropriately (no tax collected). If it returns \"invalid,\" we will include VAT and mark the invoice for dispute escalation.
- For audit trail, include a summary CSV exported from our billing system with usage rows, entity allocated, and the VIES timestamp. Ben, please add that CSV to the deliverables.

Vanessa Ortiz
